ap_calculus_ab-f02.title: Analysis from the graph of f'

stimulus.description: The function f is continuous on [0,8] and has a continuous derivative f'. The graph of f', consisting of line segments connecting the labeled points, is shown.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On what open intervals in $(0,8)$ is the graph of $f$ concave up? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: Concave up on (4,8) because f' is increasing there.

rubric_rows.criterion: Maximal open intervals where f' is increasing (adjacent intervals merged)
Reason: f' is increasing (so f'' > 0) on those intervals

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the $x$-coordinate of each point at which $f$ has a relative extremum on $(0,8)$, and classify each as a relative minimum or relative maximum. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: x = 2: relative maximum; x = 6: relative minimum because f' changes sign there.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the x-values where f' = 0 and changes sign
Classifies each using the sign change of f' (negative to positive: minimum; positive to negative: maximum)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Given that $f(0)=3$, find the value of $x$ at which $f$ attains its absolute minimum on $[0,8]$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: Candidates [0, 2, 6, 8] with f values [(0, '3'), (2, '9'), (6, '1'), (8, '3')]; absolute minimum at x = 6.

rubric_rows.criterion: Considers the relative-minimum location(s) and the endpoints as candidates
Justification: compares the values of f at all candidates, using net area under f'
Answer

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find $f(8)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses f(8) = f(0) + the integral of f' (signed areas)
Answer

stimulus.description: Slopes shown in a proposed slope field for dH/dt at selected points (t, H)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The temperature $H(t)$ of an object in a room satisfies $\dfrac{dH}{dt}=-\frac{1}{10}\,(H-20)$, where $H$ is in degrees Celsius and $t$ in minutes, with $H(0)=80$. Explain why the proposed slope field in the table could not be a slope field for this differential equation.
parts.model_answer: At (4, 25) the differential equation gives slope -0.5, but the table shows 0.5; the sign is wrong.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a point where the proposed slope disagrees in sign (or value) with dH/dt computed from the equation, using H and t values

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line tangent to the graph of $H$ at $t=0$. Show the work that leads to your answer.
parts.model_answer: dH/dt at t=0 = -6

rubric_rows.criterion: Answer with work (substitutes H(0) into the differential equation)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For $t>0$ it is known that $H(t)>20$. It can be shown that $\dfrac{d^2H}{dt^2}=\frac{1}{100}\,(H-20)$. The line tangent to the graph of $H$ at $t=0$ is used to approximate $H(4)$.
